title: Convenient, But Can it Replace the Skillet Method?
text:
Convenient, But Can it Replace the Skillet Method?. Emeson Omelet Wave is a convenient device for quick preparation of an omelet in the microwave. Its semi- circle design is made to hold and shape the eggs and other ingredients into a nicely shaped omelet, prepared and ready to eat in minutes.

I was anxious to give this product a try, just to see if it could produce an omelet not only quickly, but also one that tastes as good as those prepared on the stove top. The preparation is simple enough. You just pour the eggs and other ingredients into the plastic container and pop into the microwave. In less than two minutes, the food is ready to consume.

I have to give a product like this kudos for speed, but the omelet itself? Well, I have certainly had better. The problem is that eggs turn out more like a container of scrambled eggs than an actual omelet. They lack the shape and other qualities you expect. I agree with what others have said- the results are perfect for making a breakfast burrito because what you get is just right for scrambled egg filling. The eggs taste okay, but they don't have the slightly brown look and better flavor of an omelet prepared in a skillet.

The Emson Omelet Wave is easy to clean. Its non- stick surface and small size make it a cinch to wipe clean and it is dishwasher safe. These qualities are nice, but they are not enough to eclipse the quality of the food itself, which is okay but nothing great.

I like devices that save time and effort and this contraption is certainly more convenient than cooking on the stove top. But a skillet doesn't take that much more time and if you have your mind set on the perfect omelet, the traditional preparation is the way to go. This microwave device is acceptable and makes good scrambled eggs, but it cannot take the place of a good skillet and some old- fashioned heat.
